references.text: The Passover lamb was to be prepared and eaten at the place God had chosen, in accordance with the regulations for celebrating Passover in Egypt.
Instructions on preparing the Passover lamb—it was to be roasted over fire, a detail expanded upon in Deuteronomy with the word 'boil' or 'prepare'.
God chooses a specific place where the Israelites are to bring their offerings and hold their religious festivals.
Prohibition against eating tithes and offerings within the city gates—they must be eaten at the place the Lord chooses.
The tithe is to be eaten at the place the Lord chooses for His name to dwell there.
The Passover sacrifice is to be slaughtered at the place the Lord chooses for His name to dwell there.
During King Josiah's celebration of Passover, the Passover lamb was roasted over fire in accordance with the regulation.
